items.en: Execution and mutilation of the Batahin at Omdurman
items.ar: إعدام البطاحين وتقطيعهم في أم درمان
items.se: After Batahin tribesmen refused the Khalifa's call-up, 67 of their men were judged 'disobedient' and publicly hanged, beheaded or mutilated in the Omdurman market-place.
items.sa: بعد رفض رجال من البطاحين أوامر الخليفة بالتجنيد، حُكم على 67 رجلًا منهم بالعصيان، فشُنق بعضهم وقُطعت رؤوس آخرين وبُترت أطراف الباقين علنًا في سوق أم درمان.

items.en: Migration of the Taaisha to Omdurman and eviction of residents
items.ar: هجرة التعايشة إلى أم درمان وإخلاء سكانها
items.se: On the Khalifa's call, his Taaisha (Baggara) tribe marched through Kordofan to the White Nile and was shipped to Omdurman. Residents between the mosque and Omdurman Fort were evicted to house them, and grain was requisitioned.
items.sa: بدعوة من الخليفة، سار قومه التعايشة عبر كردفان إلى النيل الأبيض ونُقلوا إلى أم درمان، وطُرد سكان الحي الواقع بين المسجد وطابية أم درمان لإسكانهم.

s.c: Rudolf C. Slatin (tr. F. R. Wingate) (1896) Fire and Sword in the Sudan: A Personal Narrative of Fighting and Serving the Dervishes, 1879-1895
s.q: his own tribe, the Taaisha, had arrived in Omdurman

items.en: Typhoid among Mahdist troops in Darfur; famine depopulation
items.ar: التيفوئيد بين قوات المهدية في دارفور ومجاعة أخلت البلاد
items.se: Slatin reports Darfur 'almost depopulated by famine' under the emir Osman Wad Adam. A typhoid epidemic in his army forced a retreat to El Fasher, where he died.
items.sa: يذكر سلاطين أن دارفور كادت تخلو من سكانها بسبب المجاعة في عهد الأمير عثمان ود آدم، وأن وباء التيفوئيد في جيشه أجبره على التراجع إلى الفاشر حيث مات.

s.c: Rudolf C. Slatin (tr. F. R. Wingate) (1896) Fire and Sword in the Sudan: A Personal Narrative of Fighting and Serving the Dervishes, 1879-1895

items.en: Zeki Tummal's raid and massacre of the Dinka
items.ar: غارة الزاكي طمل على الدينكا ومذبحتهم
items.se: Ordered to leave Fashoda after typhus hit his army, Zeki Tummal was told by the Khalifa first to raid the Dinka, who had already submitted. The men were massacred and the women, children and cattle carried off.
items.sa: بعد تفشّي التيفوس في جيشه بفشودة، أمر الخليفة الزاكي طمل بالإغارة على الدينكا الذين كانوا قد خضعوا، فذُبح الرجال وسُبيت النساء والأطفال ونُهبت الماشية.

s.c: Rudolf C. Slatin (tr. F. R. Wingate) (1896) Fire and Sword in the Sudan: A Personal Narrative of Fighting and Serving the Dervishes, 1879-1895
s.q: seize their cattle and enslave their wives and children

items.se: At the Battle of Omdurman on 2 September 1898, the Anglo-Egyptian army destroyed the Khalifa's forces. Churchill gives the Mahdist losses as 9,700 killed, 10,000 to 16,000 wounded and 5,000 prisoners, figures computed by the victors.
items.sa: في معركة أم درمان يوم 2 سبتمبر 1898 دمّر الجيش الإنجليزي المصري قوات الخليفة. ويذكر تشرشل أن خسائر الأنصار بلغت 9700 قتيل، وما بين 10000 و16000 جريح، و5000 أسير، وهي أرقام حسبها المنتصرون.

s.c: Winston Spencer Churchill (ed. Col. F. Rhodes) (1899) The River War: An Historical Account of the Reconquest of the Soudan, Vol. II
s.q: The Dervish losses were, from computations made on the field and corrected at a later date, ascertained to be 9,700 killed, and wounded variously estimated from 10,000 to 16,000. There were, besides, 5,000 prisoners.

items.en: Turco-Egyptian slave raids (ghazwas) in the Nuba hills and beyond Fazughli
items.ar: غزوات الرقيق التركية المصرية في جبال النوبة وما وراء فازوغلي
items.se: Muhammad Ali pressed his commanders to intensify armed slave raids (ghazwas) to recruit Sudanese for his new army, sending captives to a camp at Aswan. Until 1838 hardly a year passed without raids in the Nuba hills and beyond Fazughli, and many captives died en route or at Aswan.
items.sa: ضغط محمد علي على قادته لتكثيف غزوات الرقيق المسلحة لتجنيد السودانيين في جيشه الجديد، وأُرسل الأسرى إلى معسكر في أسوان. وحتى عام 1838 لم تكد تمر سنة دون غزوات في جبال النوبة وما وراء فازوغلي، ومات كثير من الأسرى في الطريق أو في أسوان.

s.c: H.A. Ibrahim (with B.A. Ogot) The Sudan in the nineteenth century (General History of Africa VI, ch.14)
s.q: the Sudan to intensify their ghazuas - armed slave raids - and to send the greatest possible number of Africans to the camp specially made for them at Aswan

items.en: White Nile slave raiding and the Kaka slave market
items.ar: غارات الرقيق على النيل الأبيض وسوق كاكا للرقيق
items.se: From 1840 raids along the White Nile turned the slave traffic into a mass trade, run from fortified zeribas, and Baggara who could not pay cattle taxes raided the Jieng (Dinka) for slaves. Kaka in northern Shilluk country became the main White Nile slave market, selling about 2,000 slaves a year by 1860.
items.sa: منذ عام 1840 حوّلت الغارات على طول النيل الأبيض تجارة الرقيق إلى تجارة واسعة انطلاقًا من الزرائب المحصّنة، وأغار البقارة الذين عجزوا عن دفع ضرائب الماشية على الجينق (الدينكا) طلبًا للرقيق. وصارت كاكا في شمال بلاد الشلك السوق الرئيسية للرقيق على النيل الأبيض، يُباع فيها نحو 2000 رقيق سنويًا بحلول 1860.

fg.t: an average of 2000 slaves were being sold annually at Kaka

s.c: H.A. Ibrahim (with B.A. Ogot) The Sudan in the nineteenth century (General History of Africa VI, ch.14)
s.q: Frequent raids were m a d e along the White Nile for the purpose of capturing slaves, and from 1840 the traffic in h u m a n

s.c: H.A. Ibrahim (with B.A. Ogot) The Sudan in the nineteenth century (General History of Africa VI, ch.14)

items.en: Famine in Wawat (Lower Nubia) relieved with Egyptian grain
items.ar: مجاعة في واوات (النوبة السفلى) خُففت بحبوب مصرية
items.se: At the end of the Old Kingdom, the prince of Edfu recorded on his tomb at Mealla that grain was sent to Wawat in Lower Nubia to prevent famine. GHA reads this as evidence that Egypt-Nubia relations continued in the First Intermediate Period.
items.sa: في نهاية الدولة القديمة سجّل أمير إدفو على جدار مقبرته في المعلا أن الحبوب أُرسلت إلى واوات في النوبة السفلى لدرء المجاعة. وتعدّ الموسوعة ذلك دليلًا على استمرار العلاقات بين مصر والنوبة في عصر الانتقال الأول.

s.c: A.H. Zayed (with J. Dévisse) (1981) Egypt's relations with the rest of Africa, ch.4 (General History of Africa II)
s.q: grain was sent to W a w a t to prevent famine

items.en: Flight from the Gezira and Shendi during the 1822 tax revolt
items.ar: النزوح من الجزيرة وشندي إبان ثورة الضرائب عام 1822
items.se: When heavy taxes provoked revolt in February 1822, people from Shendi to Sennar fled by the thousand to the borders of Ethiopia, the Atbara valley and the Gedaref region. Ismail hurried back from Fazughli and briefly calmed the situation by revising the taxes.
items.sa: حين أشعلت الضرائب الباهظة الثورة في فبراير 1822، فرّ الناس بالآلاف من شندي إلى سنار نحو تخوم الحبشة ووادي أتبرا ومنطقة القضارف. وعاد إسماعيل مسرعًا من فازوغلي فهدّأ الوضع مؤقتًا بمراجعة الضرائب.

s.c: H.A. Ibrahim (with B.A. Ogot) The Sudan in the nineteenth century (General History of Africa VI, ch.14)
s.q: F r o m Shendi to Sennär the people fled by the thousand to the borders of Ethiopia, to the valley of Atbara and to the region of Gedaref.

items.se: The Great Famine of 1684, remembered in Arabic as Umm Laham, struck during the reign of Reth Dhokoth. It probably drove many Shilluk to flee northwards to raid or settle along the White Nile. No mortality figures are given (VERIFY).
items.sa: ضربت المجاعة الكبرى عام 1684، المعروفة بالعربية بأم لحم، في عهد الرث دوكوث. ويُرجّح أنها دفعت كثيرًا من الشلك إلى الفرار شمالًا للإغارة أو الاستقرار على النيل الأبيض. ولا تتوفر أرقام عن الضحايا (يحتاج تحقق).

s.c: Y.F. Hasan and B.A. Ogot (1992) The Sudan, 1500–1800, ch.7 (General History of Africa V)
s.q: T h e Great Famine of 1684 (Umm Laham in Arabic) was probably responsible for sending m a n y Shillukfleeingnorthwards, to raid or settle in Bahr Scheluk.

By early June, ... the number of people in need of food assistance was found to have risen to 795,000 persons.

items.ar: دارفور 2003–: قرارات ونتائج بشأن الإبادة الجماعية (منسوبة)
items.se: The US Secretary of State concluded in September 2004 that genocide had been committed in Darfur. The UN International Commission of Inquiry (S/2005/60) concluded the Government of the Sudan had NOT pursued a policy of genocide. The ICC charges Omar al-Bashir with, among other things, three counts of genocide allegedly committed between 2003 and 2008 (warrants 4 Mar 2009 and 12 Jul 2010).
items.sa: خلص وزير الخارجية الأمريكي في سبتمبر 2004 إلى وقوع إبادة جماعية في دارفور، بينما خلصت لجنة التحقيق الدولية التابعة للأمم المتحدة إلى أن حكومة السودان لم تنتهج سياسة إبادة جماعية، وتوجه المحكمة الجنائية الدولية إلى عمر البشير ثلاث تهم بالإبادة الجماعية.

s.c: Colin L. Powell, U.S. Secretary of State (2004) The Crisis in Darfur (Testimony Before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee)
s.q: I concluded, that genocide has been committed in Darfur and that the Government of Sudan and the Jingaweit bear responsibility -- and that genocide may still be occurring.

s.c: International Commission of Inquiry on Darfur (2005) Report of the International Commission of Inquiry on Darfur to the United Nations Secretary-General (S/2005/60)
s.q: 518. Conclusion. On the basis of the foregoing observations, the Commission concludes that the Government of the Sudan has not pursued a policy of genocide.

s.c: International Criminal Court Al Bashir case: The Prosecutor v. Omar Hassan Ahmad Al Bashir (ICC-02/05-01/09)
s.q: three counts of genocide: by killing, by causing serious bodily or mental harm, and by deliberately inflicting on each target group conditions of life calculated to bring about the group's physical destruction, allegedly committed at least between 2003 and 2008 in Darfur, Sudan The first warrant for arrest for Omar Hassan Ahmad Al Bashir was issued on 4 March 2009, the second on 12 July 2010.

items.se: According to the UN Panel of Experts (S/2024/65), RSF and allied militias targeted the Masalit community in West Darfur; violations may amount to war crimes and crimes against humanity. The Panel did not use the word genocide in this passage.
items.sa: وفقا لفريق خبراء الأمم المتحدة استهدفت قوات الدعم السريع والميليشيات المتحالفة معها مجتمع المساليت في غرب دارفور.

tl.t: In El Geneina alone, between 10,000 and 15,000 people were killed.

s.c: Panel of Experts on the Sudan (established pursuant to UNSC resolution 1591 (2005)) (2024) Letter dated 15 January 2024 from the Panel of Experts on the Sudan addressed to the President of the Security Council (final report)
s.q: In West Darfur (El Geneina, Sirba, Murne and Masteri), RSF and allied militias targeted the Masalit community in particular. RSF allied militias systematically violated international humanitarian law. Some of those violations may amount to war crimes and crimes against humanity. ... In El Geneina alone, between 10,000 and 15,000 people were killed.

items.ar: قرار الولايات المتحدة بشأن الإبادة الجماعية ضد الدعم السريع (يناير 2025)
items.se: On 7 January 2025 the US Secretary of State concluded that members of the RSF and allied militias have committed genocide in Sudan (US government determination).
items.sa: في 7 يناير 2025 خلص وزير الخارجية الأمريكي إلى أن أفرادا من قوات الدعم السريع والميليشيات المتحالفة ارتكبوا إبادة جماعية في السودان.

s.c: Antony J. Blinken, U.S. Secretary of State (2025) Genocide Determination in Sudan and Imposing Accountability Measures (Press Statement)
s.q: Based on this information, I have now concluded that members of the RSF and allied militias have committed genocide in Sudan.

items.en: RSF takeover of El Fasher (Oct 2025) – FFM 'hallmarks of genocide'
items.se: The UN Independent International Fact-Finding Mission for the Sudan (A/HRC/61/77, 17 Feb 2026) assessed that RSF mass killings during the takeover of El Fasher on or around 26–27 October 2025, after an 18-month siege, are 'indicators of a genocidal path' (Mission's assessment, not a court ruling).
items.sa: قدرت بعثة الأمم المتحدة المستقلة لتقصي الحقائق أن عمليات القتل الجماعي أثناء سيطرة الدعم السريع على الفاشر في 26–27 أكتوبر 2025 مؤشرات على مسار إبادة جماعية.

s.c: Independent International Fact-Finding Mission for the Sudan (2026) Sudan: Hallmarks of Genocide in El-Fasher (A/HRC/61/77, advance unedited version)
s.q: The Independent International Fact-Finding Mission for the Sudan (“the Mission”) assesses that the mass killings and related atrocities committed by the Rapid Support Forces in and around El-Fasher, during its takeover of the city on or around 26 and 27 October 2025, are indicators of a genocidal path.

items.se: Human Rights Watch (1994 report on 1991–93) states that SPLA-Nasir forces (mostly Nuer) massacred many Dinka civilians in an effort to capture Bor, which led directly to the 'Hunger Triangle' famine.

s.q: the Nasir forces (mostly Nuer) massacred many Dinka civilians in an effort to captureGarang's home territory of Bor. The massacre touched off one of the most violent periods of inter-factional and inter-tribal fighting in southern Sudan's history.

s.q: The alarming situation is manifested most recently by the seizure and occupation of the town of Heglig and its oil fields in Sudan by South Sudan’s army, the Sudan People’s Liberation Army (SPLA), the Council said in a presidential statement.

items.ar: اللاجئون من جنوب السودان في السودان
items.se: As of 30 Sep 2026, UNHCR's Sudan country portal lists 689,397 South Sudanese refugees and asylum-seekers in Sudan, the largest group; a government estimate of 1.3 million is noted by UNHCR as requiring verification.
items.sa: حتى 30 سبتمبر 2026 تدرج بوابة المفوضية 689,397 لاجئا وطالب لجوء من جنوب السودان في السودان، وهي أكبر مجموعة.

s.q: Total number of South Sudanese refugees includes UNHCR/COR registered refugees, Immigration Passport Police (IPP) registered figures and unregistered population. Additional sources estimate a total of 1.3 million South Sudanese refugees in Sudan; however, these data require verification.
